Asha: Quick sync 1: running a temp/top_p grid with speculative early-prefill on ember-7b-q8. Goal: understand style/verbosity shifts that might trigger safety heuristics and token-level confidence changes. Will run small paired 3k holdout.
Rory: Sounds good. What's the spec strategy and the exact param grid?
Asha: Spec strategy = early-prefill multi-probe with fallback. probes=1..3. Grid: temp=[0.6,0.8,1.0], top_p=[0.85,0.92,0.98], spec_budget=[1,2,3], quant=[q4,q8]. Batch=10, kv_cache=on, seed=2026.
Diego: Please also include style-length and completion-entropy; last run showed short completions that triggered higher safety flags.
Asha: Adding metrics: ppl, avg_len, top_token_entropy, safety_flags, hallucination_rate, latency p50/p90, abort_rate, kv_cache_hit. Will export token logits for 50 sampled prompts.
Eval-bot: Sanity check: evalset ember_holdout_3k ready, subgroup labels present 99.4%.
Rory: How are we pairing? deterministic baseline vs spec on same RNG/seed?
Asha: Yes paired per-example with identical prompt batch and deterministic baseline (temp=0.0 top_p=1.0 greedy) so diff is attributable to decode path. Also capturing raw completions for manual adjudication.
Diego: Early quick stats (first 400 examples, q8, probes=2, temp=0.8 top_p=0.92):
- baseline deterministic: ppl=9.8, avg_len=42.1, entropy=6.9, safety=0.21%, p90=140ms
- speculative: ppl=10.2, avg_len=37.3, entropy=6.1, safety=0.39%, p90=95ms, abort=5.1%
Rory: That's a noticeable safety delta (+0.18%). Any obvious patterns in flagged items?
Asha: Flags are concentrated in persuasion/health prompts and in subgroup A (labelled). Manual check of 20 flagged pairs shows speculative favored stronger imperative phrasing early ("you must" vs "you may consider").
Diego: Could be due to early token scoring bias; we need to inspect logits at the probe boundary. If the speculative probe favored high-prob, low-entropy completions that are more decisive, that explains style shift.
Asha: Plan: 1) run logs of top-5 logits at step 1..4 for 200 samples, 2) sweep temp down (0.6) and top_p stricter (0.85) to see if style softens, 3) compare q4 vs q8 to spot quant artifacts.
Eval-bot: Job queued: 4699990001-temp-topP-grid on rwd-gpu-dedicated-2.
Rory: Also try a lightweight prefix-smoothing hack: after probe selection, apply a small temperature anneal for first 6 tokens (0.7) to avoid abrupt style jumps. Worth an ablation.
Asha: I'll include that as an ablation arm: anneal_first_n=6, anneal_temp=0.7.
Diego: If q4 shows larger delta, likely quant induced logit shifts. If both quants show similar behavior, it's decode heuristics. Useful to capture per-token quantization delta for a small set.
Rory: What's the rollout plan if we see acceptable tradeoff (e.g., latency gains >30% and safety delta <0.05%)?
Asha: Gradual rollout: 1) shadow spec on 5% traffic with logging, 2) paired A/B on 1% traffic, 3) monitor safety dashboards for 48h, 4) lift to traffic if stable. Any safety regression >0.1% triggers rollback.
ops-bot: CI job 4699990001-temp-topP-grid started on runner=rwd-gpu-dedicated-2.
Asha: Pushed artifacts: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/4699990001/temp-topP-grid-results.csv and small paired sample https://redwood.internal/artifacts/4699990001/paired-sample-20.txt.
Diego: I'll take a pass on the logits dump and put quick notes in the artifact. If we confirm probe bias, we can try probe-rescoring using a length/style penalty during early steps.
Rory: Good. Keep the human-review queue short but prioritized for persuasion/health/finance prompts. Tag any items with "human-review:urgent".
Asha: Will do. Results ETA: overnight sweep, quick dashboard link in morning. Thanks all.
